scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Connect wallet
Sign a message
Approve
Transaction
Testnets are practice blockchains with free, worthless coins
scenes.vo: Practice run: read every prompt, do one small swap, then revoke the approval. First, Connect wallet: lets a site see your address. It can't move funds by itself. Next, Sign a message: proves you own the address (for example to log in). Read it. Some "messages" are really permissions (Lesson 1.4). Then, Approve: gives an app permission to move a specific token. Limit the amount. Also, Transaction: actually does something (swap, deposit) and costs gas. On top of that, Testnets are practice blockchains with free, worthless coins. Ethereum's main one is Sepolia. You get test ETH from a faucet (a free giveaway site). Use testnets to practise without risk.
scenes.cap: Practice run: read every prompt, do one small swap, then revoke the approval. First, Connect wallet: lets a site see your address. It can't move funds by itself. Ethereum's main one is Sepolia. You get test ETH from a faucet (a free giveaway site). Use testnets to practise without risk.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: Priya connects to a DEX on Arbitrum.
She edits it to $20, swaps $20 of USDC for ETH, pays ~$0.05 in gas, checks…
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Priya connects to a decks on Arbitrum. Her wallet shows "Approve U.S.D.C.: Unlimited". She edits it to $20, swaps $20 of U.S.D.C. for ETH, pays about $0.05 in gas, checks the transaction on the explorer, then revokes the approval. Total cost: a few cents. Total lessons learned: five.
